audit: B1 lazy-context coverage adversarial gap-hunt (11 GPU modules)
module_level_gpu_calls: all modules report NONE (import creates no CUDA context)

gaps.location: BLSMemory.allocate_data (gpuarray.zeros lines 469-471) and allocate_freqs (gpuarray.zeros lines 461-464), reached via the PUBLIC class entry BLSMemory.fromdata/__init__->setdata (cuvarbase.BLSMemory is exported in cuvarbase/__init__.py line 21)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: Neither BLSMemory.__init__, setdata, fromdata, allocate_data, nor allocate_freqs ever calls ensure_context(). A user (or the shipped docs/source/plots/benchmarks.py:102, which does `bls.BLSMemory.fromdata(t, y, dy, freqs=freqs, ...)`) can construct/populate a BLSMemory as the very first GPU activity in the process. fromdata -> setdata -> allocate_data()/allocate_freqs() hits gpuarray.zeros with no CUDA context retained, raising LogicError ('explicit_context_dependent failed: invalid device context - no currently active context?'). The prompt's premise that Memory.fromdata is 'normally reached AFTER a compile_* or process __init__' is true for the internal eebls_gpu_fast path but NOT enforced for direct public use of the exported class.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add ensure_context() at the top of BLSMemory.__init__ (mirroring GPUAsyncProcess.__init__), or at the top of allocate_data/allocate_freqs. Same for BLSBatchMemory.__init__/transfer_to_gpu in cuvarbase/memory/bls_memory.py.

gaps.location: _eebls_gpu_fast_impl: BLSMemory.fromdata/setdata at lines 593-601 when the caller passes shmem_lim explicitly (so line 591 ensure_context is skipped) AND functions resolves from a _get_cached_kernels cache HIT (so compile_bls/ensure_context at line 116/331 is also skipped)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: On a cache hit, _get_cached_kernels (lines 109-128) returns cached functions WITHOUT calling ensure_context() — it only calls compile_bls on a miss. If the caller also supplies shmem_lim, the `if shmem_lim is None` ensure_context() at line 591 is bypassed, so the first GPU op becomes BLSMemory.fromdata -> gpuarray.zeros. HOWEVER this is mitigated: a warm kernel cache can only exist if compile_bls already ran earlier in THIS process, which already called ensure_context() and cached the module in _autoctx (context persists for process lifetime). So in practice the context is always live whenever the cache is warm. Flagging as 'unsure' because the safety depends on the coupling 'cache warm => compile_bls ran => _autoctx set', which is an invariant of the current process model rather than a guarantee local to this call site.
gaps.suggested_fix: Make _get_cached_kernels call ensure_context() unconditionally before the cache lookup (cheap — it just returns the cached module after first call), so kernel acquisition self-guarantees context independent of the warm-cache invariant. Alternatively move the ensure_context() in _eebls_gpu_fast_impl out of the `if shmem_lim is None` guard so it runs on every call.

gaps.location: conditional_entropy_fast (ce.py:84-165), specifically the ensure_context() at line 98 guarded by `if shmem_lim is None` (line 97); downstream GPU work at line 103 (transfer_data_to_gpu) and line 158 (func.prepared_async_call)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: conditional_entropy_fast is part of the public API (exported in __init__.py _LAZY_ATTRS line 27). Its sole ensure_context() call sits inside the `if shmem_lim is None` branch. shmem_lim is a documented public parameter; passing any non-None value skips the only ensure_context() in the function, then proceeds to memory.transfer_data_to_gpu() (line 103) and the kernel launch (line 158) with no context guarantee from this function. A caller who has a precompiled `functions` tuple and an allocated `memory` would in practice already have a context (both require one to produce), so this is a latent/defensive gap rather than a path the bundled run() ever hits — run() is an instance method and __init__ already ensured context.
gaps.suggested_fix: Move ensure_context() to the very top of conditional_entropy_fast, unconditionally (before the `if shmem_lim is None` check), mirroring the compile_*/__init__ pattern. e.g. add `ensure_context()` as the first statement and let the get_attribute branch reuse it.

gaps.location: conditional_entropy (ce.py:29-81): memory.transfer_data_to_gpu() at line 39 and the prepared_async_call kernel launches at lines 47, 53, 63, 71, 74, 76
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: conditional_entropy is public API (exported __init__.py line 26) and contains NO ensure_context() call at all. Internally it is only invoked via self.call_func from run() (line 536), which is an instance method so __init__/ensure_context already ran — that path is safe. But the standalone exported function, called directly with a user-supplied ConditionalEntropyMemory + functions tuple, performs device transfers and kernel launches with no context guarantee of its own. As with the fast variant, a realistic caller must already hold a context to have produced `functions` (needs SourceModule via a process) and an allocated memory, so this is defensive rather than a demonstrated crash on the in-package path.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add `ensure_context()` as the first statement of conditional_entropy() for symmetry/robustness with the rest of the lazy-context refactor (compile_* and __init__ all do this). Harmless no-op when context already exists.

gaps.location: ConditionalEntropyMemory (cuvarbase/memory/ce_memory.py) allocate()/allocate_data()/allocate_bins()/allocate_freqs() — gpuarray.zeros at lines 144,145,147,160,162,165,168,178,180; and transfer/fill methods
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: ConditionalEntropyMemory is a publicly exported class (__init__.py _LAZY_ATTRS line ~19, importable as cuvarbase.ConditionalEntropyMemory). It calls gpuarray.zeros / set_async / fill / cuda.aligned_zeros directly and never calls ensure_context(). Within ce.py all construction+allocation goes through a process instance (post-ensure_context), so the in-package CE paths are safe; but a user instantiating ConditionalEntropyMemory and calling .allocate() or .fromdata() directly, without ever constructing a GPUAsyncProcess, would hit gpuarray.zeros with no active context. This is outside ce.py proper but is the backing store reached by ce.py's standalone functions.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add ensure_context() at the top of ConditionalEntropyMemory.allocate()/allocate_data() (or in its __init__) so direct use of the exported memory class is self-sufficient, consistent with how compile_* guards the standalone BLS entry points.

gaps.location: pdm_async (module-level function, lines 120-165) — direct external invocation
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: pdm_async is a module-level public function (not underscore-prefixed) and does NOT call ensure_context() itself. In principle a caller could import cuvarbase.pdm.pdm_async and invoke it directly without ever constructing PDMAsyncProcess. HOWEVER, to do so they must supply a real `stream`, a `function` (prepared kernel), and non-None gpuarrays in data_gpu — none of which can be created without an active CUDA context already existing. So the only way to build valid arguments is to have triggered ensure_context() elsewhere. This is therefore not a reachable real bug, only a theoretical untrusted-input path.
gaps.suggested_fix: Optional hardening: add ensure_context() as the first line of pdm_async() for defense-in-depth/consistency with bls.compile_* (which DO ensure_context at top), even though all valid argument-construction paths already establish the context. Not required for correctness.

gaps.location: nfft_adjoint_async (cunfft.py:25) reached with a hand-built NFFTMemory rather than via a process. nfft_adjoint_async is a public, __all__-exported symbol (__init__.py:24). NFFTMemory is ALSO a public, __all__-exported symbol (__init__.py:18,45) documented in memory/README.md as directly usable. None of NFFTMemory's GPU methods (allocate_data:85-86, allocate_precomp_psi:99-101, allocate_grid gpuarray.zeros:115 + cufft.Plan:117, allocate_pinned_cpu cuda.aligned_zeros:133, transfer_data_to_gpu set_async:211-212) nor NFFTMemory.__init__ call ensure_context(). So a user who does `mem = NFFTMemory(sigma, cuda.Stream(), m); mem.fromdata(t, y, nf=...)` and then `nfft_adjoint_async(mem, funcs)` performs the FIRST GPU op (gpuarray.zeros / cuda.Stream / cufft.Plan) with NO context retained.
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: Both nfft_adjoint_async and NFFTMemory are top-level documented public API; the docstring of nfft_adjoint_async (lines 38-41) even says memory 'must have data already set (see NFFTAsyncProcess.allocate())', acknowledging a memory built outside any process. The first GPU call on that manual path is NFFTMemory.allocate_*/cuda.Stream(), none of which ensure context. Note: the offending GPU calls physically live in memory/nfft_memory.py, not in cunfft.py lines themselves -- but the gap is *entered* through cunfft.py's public nfft_adjoint_async contract, which assumes a pre-allocated NFFTMemory and never re-checks context. Whether this is a real-world bug depends on whether any supported workflow constructs NFFTMemory directly; the v1.0 process/LS paths do not.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add ensure_context() at the top of NFFTMemory.__init__ (or at least at the start of NFFTMemory.allocate/allocate_data/allocate_grid/transfer_data_to_gpu in memory/nfft_memory.py), so manual NFFTMemory use cannot reach gpuarray.zeros/cufft.Plan/cuda.Stream without a retained primary context. Cheap (cached after first call) and closes the only path into nfft_adjoint_async that bypasses a process __init__.

gaps.location: nfft_adjoint_async (cunfft.py:25) itself does not call ensure_context() at its top, unlike bls.compile_* / tls.compile_tls which were given a top-of-function ensure_context(). It relies entirely on the precondition that `memory` and `functions` were produced under a context.
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: Defense-in-depth observation rather than a proven reachable gap: on every traced in-tree path (NFFTAsyncProcess.run, LombScargle) the memory/functions were built under a context, so context is in fact live. But because it is a documented standalone public entry point, it has no self-guard analogous to the compile_* functions, so its safety is inherited from callers rather than enforced locally.
gaps.suggested_fix: Optionally add ensure_context() at the top of nfft_adjoint_async for symmetry with bls/tls compile_* guards; harmless (idempotent/cached) and makes the standalone entry self-defending if NFFTMemory is later guarded so that a manual-memory path can no longer reach an unguarded GPU op.

gaps.location: LombScargleMemory.__init__ (cuvarbase/memory/lombscargle_memory.py:103 gpuarray.zeros, and :117 reg_g.set_async) -- the class is publicly exported as cuvarbase.LombScargleMemory (__init__.py:20,47; memory/__init__.py:16,24)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: LombScargleMemory is a public, lazily-importable top-level symbol. A user (or any standalone use of lomb_scargle_async) can construct it directly: `from cuvarbase import LombScargleMemory; LombScargleMemory(sigma, stream, m, ...)`. Its __init__ unconditionally calls gpuarray.zeros(2*nharmonics+1) at line 103 (and set_async at 117 if amplitude_prior is given). Neither the class, the memory package, nor the cuvarbase package __getattr__ ever calls ensure_context(). Constructing it WITHOUT first constructing a *AsyncProcess (the only things that ensure context) hits gpuarray.zeros with no active CUDA context -> LogicError/launch failure. The refactor moved context retention into GPUAsyncProcess.__init__/compile_* but left the public Memory classes' allocating __init__ uncovered.
gaps.suggested_fix: Call ensure_context() at the top of LombScargleMemory.__init__ (and NFFTMemory's allocate_data/allocate_grid/allocate_precomp_psi), or have the memory package gate first GPU touch. Minimal: add `from ..base import ensure_context; ensure_context()` before the gpuarray.zeros at lombscargle_memory.py:103. This also closes the analogous standalone path through lomb_scargle_async().

gaps.location: NFFTMemory allocate methods (cuvarbase/memory/nfft_memory.py:85-86,99-101 gpuarray.zeros; :115 gpuarray.zeros; :117 cufft.Plan) -- NFFTMemory is publicly exported (cuvarbase.NFFTMemory)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: Same class of hole as LombScargleMemory: NFFTMemory is public and constructible directly, and a user can call mem.allocate()/allocate_grid() without ever constructing an NFFTAsyncProcess. cufft.Plan (line 117) and gpuarray.zeros (85,99,115) need an active context, but no ensure_context() exists anywhere in nfft_memory.py. Inside lombscargle.py these are only reached via instance methods (safe), so this is strictly the directly-constructed-Memory escape hatch, not a lombscargle.py internal-path bug.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add ensure_context() at the top of NFFTMemory.allocate()/allocate_data()/allocate_grid() (or its __init__) so directly-constructed memory objects retain the context before the first gpuarray.zeros/cufft.Plan.

gaps.location: lomb_scargle_async (cuvarbase/lombscargle.py:292) and the standalone NFFT helpers it calls -- no ensure_context() of their own
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: lomb_scargle_async is a public top-level symbol (cuvarbase.lomb_scargle_async, __init__.py:29). It performs prepared kernel launches (lines 378,413) and transfers. It is 'safe' ONLY transitively: it requires a fully-allocated LombScargleMemory and prepared `functions`, which today can only come from a process that already ensured context -- EXCEPT that the public LombScargleMemory constructor (see first gap) is the very thing that lacks the guard. So if the Memory-class hole is fixed by allowing construction without context, this function would still launch kernels with no ensure_context() of its own. It is reachable from a public API without ensure_context having provably run on its own behalf; it inherits safety only from a guard that lives in a sibling class.
gaps.suggested_fix: Defensively add ensure_context() at the top of lomb_scargle_async() (cheap, idempotent, cached). This makes the standalone public entry self-sufficient rather than depending on the caller having constructed a process first. Same recommendation for cunfft.nfft_adjoint_async and cufinufft_backend.cufinufft_nfft_adjoint if they are advertised as standalone.

gaps.location: TLSMemory.allocate_gpu_arrays (lines 294-303, gpuarray.zeros), reached from TLSMemory.__init__/setdata/fromdata. TLSMemory has NO ensure_context() call anywhere.
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: TLSMemory is a public class. Constructing it and calling setdata()/fromdata() (or just fromdata with default transfer=True) reaches allocate_gpu_arrays -> gpuarray.zeros with no ensure_context() on the path. The refactor removed the module-top `import pycuda.autoprimaryctx` that previously made this implicitly safe, so on a fresh interpreter that only imported cuvarbase.tls (no compile_tls / no GPUAsyncProcess subclass — tls.py has none) there is no active primary context. Existing tests test_tls_basic.py:349-350 (test_memory_setdata) and :364 (test_memory_fromdata) exercise exactly this and are NOT gated behind PYCUDA_AVAILABLE, i.e. the project treats TLSMemory construction as context-free, which is no longer true for the device gpuarray ops. Note transfer=False does NOT avoid it: setdata at line 357 allocates gpuarrays unconditionally (the guard is `if self.t_g is None`, independent of transfer).
gaps.suggested_fix: Add `ensure_context()` as the first statement of TLSMemory.__init__ (mirroring GPUAsyncProcess.__init__), or at minimum at the top of allocate_gpu_arrays(), set_template(), and transfer_to_gpu/from_gpu. Putting it in __init__ is the cleanest and matches the base-class pattern; it makes every TLSMemory device op provably context-guarded regardless of entry path.

gaps.location: tls_search_gpu kernel=<precompiled>, memory=None path (line 561 `if kernel is None:` is False so compile_tls/ensure_context at 561-563 is skipped; then line 566 `if memory is None:` builds TLSMemory.fromdata -> gpuarray.zeros at 294-303)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: If a user passes a kernel argument but no memory, ensure_context() is never called inside tls_search_gpu before the gpuarray allocations at line 567. This is only safe if the passed kernel came from compile_tls/_get_cached_kernels (which ran ensure_context and created the global primary context). That holds for normal usage, but tls_search_gpu does not enforce or document it — a caller assembling a kernel object differently, or any future code path, would allocate device memory with no context. This is the same underlying defect as the TLSMemory gap: nothing in the memory layer self-guards.
gaps.suggested_fix: Either guard TLSMemory (preferred — see above, which fully closes this path too) or add an unconditional `ensure_context()` near the top of tls_search_gpu (e.g. right after the shared-memory budget check at line 559, before any memory/kernel branch). The latter is a one-line belt-and-suspenders fix that makes tls_search_gpu safe for every argument combination.

gaps.location: TLSMemory.allocate_pinned_arrays cuda.aligned_zeros (lines 246-285)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: Reached from TLSMemory.__init__ with no ensure_context. Listed for completeness because the docstring/attribute names call this 'pinned memory', which WOULD require a context if it used cuda.pagelocked_*/register_host_memory. As written it uses cuda.aligned_zeros, a host-only aligned allocation that does NOT require a CUDA context, so this is not an actual runtime gap today.
gaps.suggested_fix: No fix strictly required (aligned_zeros is context-free). If the suggested ensure_context() is added to TLSMemory.__init__ this is moot. Be careful not to 'upgrade' these to true pinned memory (pagelocked) later without first guaranteeing a context — that would turn this benign site into a hard gap.

gaps.location: cufinufft_nfft_adjoint (cufinufft_backend.py:90-196) — the whole function body, in particular the unconditional GPU sites at lines 171, 174, 177, 181/65, 182, 183, 191
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: cufinufft_nfft_adjoint is a public, module-level entry point. It is exported (cuvarbase.cufinufft_backend.cufinufft_nfft_adjoint; the module is listed in cuvarbase/__init__.py _SUBMODULES) and the project's own tests call it standalone on a hand-built memory object (cuvarbase/tests/test_lombscargle.py:489-491,498-501,510), so direct use is a supported pattern. The function does NOT call ensure_context() anywhere, and unlike the BLS/TLS standalone funcs it does NOT call any compile_* that would. Its `memory` argument (NFFTMemory / LombScargleMemory) does not establish context either: neither class' __init__ nor allocate()/allocate_data()/allocate_grid() calls ensure_context() (grep over cuvarbase/memory/ shows no ensure_context/autoprimaryctx). So `NFFTMemory(...); mem.fromdata(...); cufinufft_nfft_adjoint(mem)` runs gpuarray.zeros, gpuarray elementwise ops, a cufinufft.Plan, setpts/execute, and a D2D copy with no proof a CUDA context was ever retained/pushed. The refactor relocated context establishment into GPUAsyncProcess.__init__ and the compile_* functions; this module-level helper was not given an ensure_context() call and is reachable bypassing both.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add `from .base import ensure_context` and call `ensure_context()` as the first statement of cufinufft_nfft_adjoint (immediately before or after check_cufinufft(), at cufinufft_backend.py:143). This makes the standalone public entry point self-sufficient and matches the pattern used in bls.compile_* / tls.compile_tls. (Note: the parallel custom-NFFT helper nfft_adjoint_async in cunfft.py has the same standalone exposure and likely needs the same guard, but that is outside this file's scope.) The on-process path is already safe via GPUAsyncProcess.__init__, so this is only an issue for callers who use the memory + free-function API directly rather than LombScargleAsyncProcess.

gaps.location: cuvarbase/bls.py eebls_gpu_batch (def at line 2089) feeding BLSBatchMemory.transfer_to_gpu / transfer_to_cpu in cuvarbase/memory/bls_memory.py (gpuarray.zeros 185-193, set_async 195-202, get_async/get 207/210), with the first fault actually at cuda.Stream() bls.py:2194
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: eebls_gpu_batch has no unconditional ensure_context() call. The only two context-establishing calls are both conditional: compile_bls_batch() (bls.py:2168, calls ensure_context at 2062) runs only `if functions is None` (line 2167), and ensure_context().device (bls.py:2177) runs only `if shmem_lim is None` (line 2176). A public call eebls_gpu_batch(lightcurves, freqs, functions=<precompiled>, shmem_lim=<int>) skips BOTH guards, so cuda.Stream() at 2194, BLSBatchMemory.transfer_to_gpu() at 2216, and transfer_to_cpu() at 2238 all execute with no ensure_context() proven to have run on this path. (BLSBatchMemory.__init__'s aligned_zeros are host-only and safe; the device ops in transfer_to_gpu/cpu are the exposed sites.)
gaps.suggested_fix: Add an unconditional `ensure_context()` as the first statement of eebls_gpu_batch (cuvarbase/bls.py:2148), mirroring the standalone entry functions eebls_gpu (bls.py:1723) and eebls_gpu_custom (bls.py:2062-style) which call it up front. Cheap and idempotent because ensure_context() caches _autoctx. Optionally also call ensure_context() at the top of BLSBatchMemory.transfer_to_gpu()/transfer_to_cpu() so the publicly-exported BLSBatchMemory class is self-protecting regardless of caller. Note: real-world impact is limited because the legitimate way to obtain `functions` is to call compile_bls_batch() first, which already runs ensure_context() and sets the process-global cache; the gap is a latent contract hole (stale/foreign `functions`, or a caller that hand-builds the dict) rather than a guaranteed crash in the normal single-process flow.

gaps.location: Whole module: ce_memory.py never calls ensure_context(); public class ConditionalEntropyMemory.allocate()/fromdata() (and via them allocate_data line 144, allocate_bins line 160, allocate_freqs line 178)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: ConditionalEntropyMemory is a first-class public export (cuvarbase.ConditionalEntropyMemory per __init__.py line 19, and cuvarbase.memory.ConditionalEntropyMemory per memory/__init__.py line 14 / __all__). A user can construct it directly -- __init__ (lines 36-85) does only numpy/attribute work, no GPU, so it succeeds with no context -- then call mem.fromdata(t, y, nf=..., freqs=...) or mem.allocate(nf=...). allocate() (line 182) unconditionally calls allocate_data/allocate_bins/allocate_freqs, each of which calls gpuarray.zeros(...) with NO ensure_context() ever having run. The refactor only added ensure_context() to GPUAsyncProcess.__init__ and the compile_* functions; it did not add it to the memory class, which is independently public.
gaps.suggested_fix: Call ensure_context() at the top of the memory entry points that first touch the device -- minimally allocate() (covers allocate_data/bins/freqs) and the transfer_*/set_gpu_arrays_to_zero methods -- or, simplest and cheapest, add `from ..base import ensure_context` and call it once at the top of ConditionalEntropyMemory.__init__ so any directly-constructed memory object has a retained context before any of its GPU methods run. (The all-process workflow is already safe; this only closes the manual/standalone-memory public path.)

gaps.location: ConditionalEntropyMemory.transfer_data_to_gpu (212), transfer_freqs_to_gpu (237), transfer_ce_to_cpu (241), set_gpu_arrays_to_zero (349) -- public methods that issue set_async/get_async/fill
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: These are public methods on the public ConditionalEntropyMemory class. A user driving the memory object manually (the documented per-lightcurve memory pattern) can call them after allocate() without any process. None of them, nor any of their internal callers in ce.py (conditional_entropy / conditional_entropy_fast are themselves public module-level functions exported as cuvarbase.conditional_entropy / cuvarbase.conditional_entropy_fast, __init__.py lines 26-27), calls ensure_context(). conditional_entropy_fast guards only its OWN device-attribute read at line 98 (ensure_context().device for MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK) -- that single guarded read does not protect the memory.transfer_data_to_gpu() call that immediately follows it at line 103, nor the kernel launches; it merely happens to ensure context as a side effect IF shmem_lim is None, but a caller passing shmem_lim skips even that.
gaps.suggested_fix: Either guard the memory transfer/fill methods with ensure_context() (or guard them transitively via __init__ as above), and/or add ensure_context() at the top of the public standalone functions conditional_entropy and conditional_entropy_fast in ce.py so the documented `conditional_entropy(memory, functions, ...)` entry point is self-protecting rather than relying on shmem_lim being None.

gaps.location: Reliance on caller for the standalone functions conditional_entropy (ce.py:29) and conditional_entropy_fast (ce.py:84)

gaps.location: LombScargleMemory.__init__, line 103 (gpuarray.zeros for self.reg_g); secondarily line 117 (reg_g.set_async when amplitude_prior given)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: LombScargleMemory is a top-level public export (cuvarbase.LombScargleMemory, listed in __all__ of cuvarbase/__init__.py:47 and cuvarbase/memory/__init__.py:24). gaps.suggested_fix: Add a call to ensure_context() (from ..base import ensure_context, or ..core) at the very top of LombScargleMemory.__init__, before line 103. This matches the pattern already used for compile_* functions and GPUAsyncProcess.__init__. The same fix transitively protects allocate_data/allocate_grids/allocate (and the NFFTMemory cufft.Plan at nfft_memory.py:117), since those are only reachable after __init__. Consider also guarding NFFTMemory.__init__ similarly for symmetry (it does no alloc itself, but its allocate* methods at nfft_memory.py:85-118 -- gpuarray.zeros + cufft.Plan -- are publicly reachable on a standalone NFFTMemory the same way; NFFTMemory is likewise a top-level public export).

gaps.location: LombScargleMemory public allocation methods reachable standalone: allocate_data (l.138-140), allocate_grids (l.188 + delegated cufft.Plan), allocate (l.256), fromdata (l.360)
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: These are public instance methods. On the normal process path they are context-safe (downstream of __init__ line 103, which itself requires a context). The methods themselves contain no independent ensure_context() guard, so they rely entirely on __init__ having forced a context. Fixing __init__ (above) closes this; without that fix these are additional unguarded device-alloc / cufft.Plan sites.
gaps.suggested_fix: Covered by fixing LombScargleMemory.__init__ (and NFFTMemory.__init__). No separate guard needed if __init__ ensures context, since these methods cannot run before __init__.

gaps.location: NFFTMemory class as a whole (public API): cuvarbase.NFFTMemory(...).allocate()/fromdata()/allocate_data()/allocate_grid()/allocate_precomp_psi()/transfer_data_to_gpu()/transfer_nfft_to_cpu() — i.e. every GPU site at nfft_memory.py lines 85-86, 99-101, 115, 117, 211-212, 216 (and dispatchers allocate@174 / fromdata@219).
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: NFFTMemory is an exported, documented public class: it is in cuvarbase/__init__.py __all__ (line 45) and _LAZY_ATTRS (line 18), and in cuvarbase/memory/__init__.py __all__/_LAZY_ATTRS, so `from cuvarbase import NFFTMemory` works. The lazy-context refactor added ensure_context() ONLY to GPUAsyncProcess.__init__, the bls/tls compile_* functions, and bls/ce device-attribute reads. It did NOT add ensure_context() to ANY Memory class (verified: zero matches for ensure_context/autoprimaryctx in the whole cuvarbase/memory/ subpackage). NFFTMemory.__init__ does no GPU work, so constructing it succeeds with no context; then the FIRST GPU call (e.g. gpuarray.zeros in allocate_data) runs with no pushed primary context. Since `import cuvarbase` no longer creates a context (that is the explicit goal of base/context.py), a fresh-interpreter sequence `import cuvarbase; m = cuvarbase.NFFTMemory(2, None, 4); m.allocate(n0=10, nf=16)` reaches gpuarray.zeros / cufft.Plan with no active context and raises pycuda LogicError 'invalid device context - no currently active context'. The same applies to building one and calling transfer_*/fromdata directly.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add `from ..base import ensure_context` and call `ensure_context()` at the top of the methods that perform the first GPU work — minimally NFFTMemory.allocate_data, allocate_precomp_psi, allocate_grid, transfer_data_to_gpu, and transfer_nfft_to_cpu (or simply at the top of allocate() and fromdata(), plus the two transfer_* methods, since allocate()/fromdata() are the documented public allocation entry points and the transfer_* methods can in principle be invoked first). This mirrors what the refactor already did for the process classes and compile_* functions, closing the only NFFTMemory-side path that bypasses context creation. Severity is edge-case rather than blocker because the normal/supported usage is through NFFTAsyncProcess/LombScargleAsyncProcess, whose __init__ runs ensure_context before any NFFTMemory method; the gap only bites a user who hand-builds NFFTMemory (a path the public export and class docstring nonetheless invite).

gaps.location: cufinufft_backend.cufinufft_nfft_adjoint (public, exported in cuvarbase.cufinufft_backend) operating on a directly-built NFFTMemory — reaches NFFTMemory.transfer_data_to_gpu (line 146) and NFFTMemory.transfer_nfft_to_cpu (line 194), plus cufinufft.Plan/gpuarray.zeros in the backend.
gaps.why_reachable_without_context: cufinufft_nfft_adjoint takes a precompiled `memory` arg and is reachable in supported use only via LombScargleAsyncProcess.run -> lomb_scargle_async (post-ensure_context). But it is itself an importable function, and if a user passes a hand-built NFFTMemory it inherits the same no-context exposure as the direct-NFFTMemory gap above (transfer_data_to_gpu's set_async, the backend's own gpuarray.zeros/cufinufft.Plan, then transfer_nfft_to_cpu). This is a consequence of the NFFTMemory gap rather than a separate defect in nfft_memory.py, but it widens the surface that reaches the unprotected NFFTMemory transfer methods.
gaps.suggested_fix: Closing the NFFTMemory gap above (ensure_context in the transfer_* methods) also covers this surface, since cufinufft_nfft_adjoint's first device touch on the memory object is memory.transfer_data_to_gpu(). Optionally also call ensure_context() at the top of cufinufft_nfft_adjoint for defense in depth (out of scope for nfft_memory.py itself).

resolution: ensure_context() added to all 6 *Memory __init__ (closes both blockers + memory edge-cases), _get_cached_kernels (cache-hit path), and cufinufft_nfft_adjoint. Standalone CE/PDM/LS/NFFT functions covered transitively (require pre-built memory+compiled kernels, both self-ensuring).
